decisions.reason: As a newly launched dental consumable with its own page and clear fit to the firm's thermoforming and laboratory workflow capabilities, it is likely to stay while management uses organisational slack to learn about demand.

This PETG thermoforming blank closely matches the firm's materials business and digital-production orientation, so unless results fall clearly below aspiration it would normally be retained for further market development.

Because the UV-curing lacquer was only mentioned rather than prominently featured, management would see weaker early evidence and a higher risk of falling short of aspiration, but a large established firm would still likely continue it for now.

The intraoral contrast spray supports clinical and digital workflow use cases and had dedicated web presentation, making it a strong strategic fit that management would be unlikely to withdraw so soon after launch.

The custom earmold line fits the firm's hearing-care customer base and custom manufacturing strengths, so even with modest early visibility it would likely be kept while performance information accumulates.

Custom hearing protection earmolds are somewhat more niche, but they still leverage the firm's earmold capabilities and channels, so boundedly rational management would usually keep them unless early results were clearly disappointing.
